name: Lennox Head
closed:
# Lennox Head Flying Site - Ballina Class D Airspace Changes 

# All Flying at Lennox Head as of the 9th of July 2026 is to cease until further notice by order of CASA and Air Services Australia.

New controlled airspace will come into effect at Ballina Airport from 9 July 2026, with
the introduction of Class D controlled airspace extending over the Lennox Head flying
site. This change will significantly affect hang gliding and paragliding operations at
Lennox Head.

The Northern Rivers Hang Gliding and Paragliding Club (NRHGPGC) has applied to the
Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) for exemptions that would allow continued hang
gliding and paragliding operations within the new Class D airspace - These applications
are currently under assessment.

Until these exemptions have been considered and approved, no hang gliding or
paragliding operations are to take place at Lennox Head. Accordingly, the site will
be closed to all flying activities from Thursday, 9 July 2026 until further notice. This
applies to all pilots, including local, interstate and international visitors.

NRHGPGC, SAFA, CASA and Airservices Australia are continuing to work together to
establish an operational framework that will enable the site to reopen safely and legally
under the new airspace arrangements. Recent correspondence indicates that CASA is
currently assessing the exemption application.

While this process is underway, it is critically important that pilots respect the closure as
any flying activity from Lennox Head while the exemption applications are under
consideration could jeopardise the approval process and may result in the withdrawal of
the applications, placing future access to the site at risk.

Further information will be provided as soon as the exemption process has been
finalised and an outcome is known. Pilots are encouraged to monitor club website and
Australian National Site Guide for updates.

Northern Rivers Hang Gliding and Paragliding Club

name: Arthurs Seat
closed:
This site is currently prohibited by Parks Victoria.
  
VHPA does not contest the closure of this site.  There is no bombout.  The LZ is a long glide away.  Pilot miscalculation, or changes in conditions causing loss of height or penetration increase the risk of unsafe landing or emergency landing in a built up area.  The VHPA's view is that the risks associated with this site outweigh the benefits.  The local club advises that an an informal CFI, SSO, SO and experienced Pilot inspection circa 2020 found that ongoing urban encroachment and road development as well as flora growth & regrowth combined to make this site less viable than when it was when first closed.
  
The National Parks Act 1975, Part 1, 4(a)(iii)provides for the use and enjoyment of those parks by the public for inspiration, solitude and appropriate self-reliant recreation.
  
This site is managed by Parks Victoria under the National Parks Act 1975. This site has been temporarily prohibited for use by Parks Victoria. Should you choose to launch from this site you may be in breach of the National Parks (Park) regulations 2003, Part 2, section 44(2) "A person must not, in a Park- (a) launch or land an aircraft."

name: Mentone
closed:
Within controlled airspace around Moorabbin airport. As per Section 4.7 (e), Section 6.5.10 and Section 6.5.11 of the [SAFA Operations Manual](http://members.safa.asn.au/isonic-downloaddoc.php?docid=0X0X1X1X47R2hYQ2t5YU9HL0xlL1RBbjlrM1VEdz09), flying within 16 km of a controlled aerodrome or below 3000 feet within 8 km of an aerodrome with regular public transport services is prohibited. This is regardless of whether flights are below 300 feet or greater than 25 metres from roads or buildings.

In 2010, the VHPA applied for an exemption for this site. CASA declined, stating: "The area surrounding Red Bluff and Mentone is one of high traffic density with both fixed wing and helicopter traffic transiting, often at 500 to 600 feet, as well as being in close proximity to final approach of the NDB A approach. Given these circumstances and the potential impact on the safety of other airspace users CASA cannot approve the establishment of hang gliding and paragliding operations at these locations, even with the controls proposed in your application."

name: Stirlings
closed: The biggest hills in the southwest, but access for flying has not been agreed with the National Park authorities.The National Park Management plan specifically forbids flying from Bluff Knoll and Hamilla Hill, although it has been flown from in the past. The Park management plan has provision to work with the HGAWA to approve flying sites in the Park in future. Please contact the HGAWA if .you are interested in doing this. The peaks are mostly covered with low scrub, in a few places it is possible for a paraglider to launch if you don't mind the possibility of line damage. Landing options are also few and far between, but there are some old gravel pits beside the main roads which provide reasonable landing grounds. The National Park does not permit landing in car parks or on roads. Towing up nearby and trying to thermal across the ranges is an option, but landings areas could still be a problem. Be aware of sailplanes coming off tow from Cranbrook and riding the ridge lift.
